questions.question: Determine whether the series converges conditionally, absolutely, or diverges.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Two-step takedown. AST gives the nod, but strip the signs and the series explodes—bigger than harmonic. Conditional convergence. Clean combo.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: You let the alternating shield fool you. Underneath, the terms tower over harmonic. Overconfidence left your flank wide open.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio lim=1. Blade skids off harmlessly. Good call not forcing it, but don't linger.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Once ln n flexes past 1, every term towers over the p=1/2 series. That one diverges, so this monster crushes. Diverges.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: Limit blasts to infinity. Heavy, but still lands the same blow. A slower sure-kill.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Smaller than harmonic doesn't prove convergence. You feinted in the wrong direction. Narrow miss.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: You picked a p=5/4 blade. The ln n melts under that power. Converges. Surgical.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: ∫ ln x / x^{3/2} converges. Longer march, but the result stands. Solid backup.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: ln n makes it bigger, not smaller. You sized up the wrong enemy—and got punished.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Two-phase strike. Without signs, it's a ln n/n beast—divergent. AST tames it. Conditional convergence.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: You killed the unarmored form but forgot it had a second phase. Alternating saves it. Don't sheathe early.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Divide and conquer. Both pieces are pinned under p>1 series. Converges. Efficient.

moves.name: Limit Comparison Test
moves.professor: One clean swing with a heavier blade. Works.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Bounded by a p=2 series. Converges. Sharp read.

moves.name: Integral Test
moves.professor: Heavy but valid. Works just fine.

moves.name: p-Series Test
moves.professor: Shifting the index doesn't touch convergence. Don't psych yourself out—trust the rules.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Classic conditional. AST holds, absolute crumbles. Textbook two-step.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio lim=1. Weapon bounces. You know when to drop it.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: You looked only at the absolute—forgot the alternating shield. Unforced error.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Same rhythm as before. AST green, absolute red. Conditional convergence. Solid.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Limit 1—dull blade. Good impulse to switch away.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Root Test rips that exponent wide open. Absolute convergence. Clean dismantle.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Also works. A different blade, same kill.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: AST would smell convergence, but Root Test reveals it's absolute. Deeper recon.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio Test feasts on factorials. Limit 1/2. Converges. Perfect matchup.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Trying to Root Test here is like bringing a catapult to a duel—technically works, but Ratio's the specialist.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: Denominator grows too slowly for that comparison. Misjudged the scale.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Factorial outruns the exponential. Ratio slams to zero. Converges. Quick and decisive.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Works, but Ratio dances through factorials smoother.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio Test doesn't even flinch at the alternating sign. Absolute convergence. Full clear.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: AST would give conditional, but Ratio secures absolute—total victory.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: p=2 at both ends. [1,3]. Endpoints secured. Territory complete.

moves.name: Endpoint Check
moves.professor: You claimed the interior but forgot the borders. Endpoints can still draw blood.

moves.name: Radius Test
moves.professor: The n/(n+1) factor doesn't touch the radius. Radius 1/2. Clean cut.

moves.name: Root Test
moves.professor: Also yields 1/2. Different weapon, same number.

moves.name: Radius Test
moves.professor: Factorial in the denominator swallows any power of x. Infinite radius. Done.

moves.name: Geometric Series Test
moves.professor: Not geometric. Wrong playbook.

moves.name: Direct Comparison Test
moves.professor: |cos n| ≤ 1, so it's trapped under a geometric series. Absolute convergence. Simple cage.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: cos n doesn't alternate neatly. Wrong tool for the job.

moves.name: nth-Term Test
moves.professor: Terms do tend to zero, so nth-Term Test shrugs. You got no intel.

questions.question: Find the sum using known series.

moves.name: Known Series Recognition
moves.professor: That's the sin series singing. Sum is √3/2. Instant recognition.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Tells you it converges, but won't whisper the sum. Right track, wrong goal.

questions.question: Find the series representation and its interval.

moves.name: Geometric Series Test
moves.professor: Factor 1/4, see 1/(1 - x/4). Geometric from there. (-4,4). Quick and polished.

moves.name: Term-by-Term Integration
moves.professor: Way too heavy. You tried to tunnel through a hill when a path was right there.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Ratio lim = 1/2 < 1. Fastest draw. Converges.

moves.name: Ratio Test
moves.professor: Also quick. Ratio just flows a heartbeat faster here.

moves.name: Alternating Series Test
moves.professor: Centered at 1, radius 1. Endpoint x=2 yields alternating harmonic, x=0 diverges. (0,2]. Clean sweep.

moves.name: Endpoint Check
moves.professor: You mapped the interior but ignored the edge. Lost half the territory.
